issue.title: Pager time-band diff-range PNG goldens flake on span-free prose base-style race
issue.description:
## Flake report

- **Test:** `tests/pager/visual/test_time_band_png_snapshots.py::test_time_band_png_snapshot[diff-range-False-size0]` (all four diff-range params flake: dark/light x 120x40/60x30)
- **Repro:** `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/pager/visual/test_time_band_png_snapshots.py -q -p no:randomly -m visual -k "diff-range"` repeated solo; also flakes under xdist

Fail/pass observations: ~50% fail rate solo on an unchanged tree (observed 4/6, 2/6, 1/6 mixes across batches); passes on immediate rerun. Failing frames show terminal-fallback white body prose where the golden shows the applied theme foreground (#e0e0e0 dark / #1f1f1f light); ~25k material pixels over the body rows. No product behavior is wrong in either frame (both readable; white exceeds contrast).

Proven pre-existing on clean master (verified via `git stash push --keep-index`): the same test fails on HEAD (additionally the committed goldens are footer-stale there: they show `( v1 -) v3 -} now - = diff` while current code renders `( v3 -) now - = read`), and master actual PNGs differ run-to-run (md5 differs, white vs #e0e0e0 prose), so the frame race predates the pager-readability work.

Root-cause analysis (all verified by execution, not just reading):
- Diff-view sections correctly skip syntax preparation (`_document_has_pending_syntax_work` and `_prepared_section_texts` skip `view == "diff"`), so the diff-range body prose is span-free; gutter spans are the only explicit spans (verified by dumping composed-body spans).
- Syntax-prep state is quiescent (`_syntax_prepared` empty, no pass running) across 6s watches; theme object is constant from mount (`textual-dark`, fg #e0e0e0); screen/widget computed colors are stable.
- The rendered fill of the span-free prose varies per process (white vs theme fg) while all live state is stable, pointing at Textual's first-paint base-style resolution (`get_visual_style` first-computation caching) racing async stylesheet application. The `wait_for`-style barriers that work for every other pager visual (they wait on syntax preparation) cannot apply here because no syntax pass ever runs for diff views.
- Barrier variants tried without success: bare pause, 0.5s delay, wait-for-first-paint, export-fill polling, `refresh(layout=True)`, subtree `notify_style_update` + repaint, recompose-until-correct loop, pinning inline prose color. None converge; several made it worse. constat: no test-side barrier tried is deterministic.
- PYTHONHASHSEED=0 fixed still flakes (not hash ordering); back-to-back exports within one settled process are stable (render path itself is deterministic given state).

Fixed alongside (not part of this bead): the stale diff-range footer in the committed goldens was regenerated to current deterministic behavior via `tools/fix_tui_screenshots`, and the neutral history-strip chrome from the pager-readability plan was accepted into the same goldens after PNG inspection.

Suggested remediation: give the diff-range body deterministic explicit styling (e.g., paint the read-fallback prose with the resolved presentation foreground instead of relying on Textual base-style inheritance), or add a Textual-level post-theme repaint hook the test can await. Either needs a plan; do not paper over with tolerances or deselection.

issue.creation_reason: Pre-existing visual flake (proven on clean master) intersected the pager-readability landing: diff-range goldens nondeterministically capture terminal-fallback white vs applied-theme prose. Recording with full root-cause evidence so it tracks as follow-up instead of blocking the plan.

payload.description: sibling pager visual-golden race in the time-band suite; a shared capture barrier may fix both

evidence.note: Relayed by sase-1es.land from sase-1es.6 note #2 (2026-10-02): during the pager virtual-body visual check, one of the 18 timeband goldens flipped between a 111px and a ~26k px diff from run to run on identical code. That matches this diff-range base-style race. No golden was touched.
